title: Reading & Use of English
paragraphs: My name is Aliya Dzhaksybekova. I am twenty-two years old and I study Environmental Science at WKU in Uralsk. I come from Karagandy — a city in the centre of Kazakhstan that is known for its industrial history and its dramatic change of seasons. For much of the twentieth century, Karagandy was one of the largest coal-mining cities in the Soviet Union. Many of my relatives worked in the mines. My grandfather was a miner for thirty-two years.

When I was growing up, I noticed something that many of my classmates had accepted as normal: the air in Karagandy was not always clean. On some mornings in winter, when coal was burned for heating, a grey haze hung over the city. By the time I was twelve, I had already begun asking why. My parents told me it had always been this way. My grandfather told me it had not — that the air had been much cleaner when he was young, before the Soviet industrial expansion.

I came to WKU to study environmental science because I wanted to understand what was happening to the air, the water, and the land around me — and because I wanted to do something about it. During my three years here, I have learned an enormous amount. I have studied climate modelling, pollution measurement, and conservation biology. Furthermore, I have completed two research internships — one at the Karagandy Environment Agency and one with a WKU project studying the impact of industrial dust on agricultural soil.

The research I am most proud of was conducted last summer with a team of four WKU students. We collected soil and air samples from ten sites around Karagandy over six weeks. The samples were analysed in the WKU laboratory, and the results were striking: heavy metal concentrations in the soil near the former mine sites were significantly above the safe limits defined by Kazakhstani environmental law. Although the mines had been closed for over twenty years, the contamination had not been remediated.

By the time we submitted our findings to the Karagandy Environment Agency, we had been working on the project for three months. The report was received with interest, and two of our recommendations have since been adopted: an independent audit of former mine sites in the region will be conducted next year, and a community monitoring programme is being established, in which local residents will be trained to measure pollution levels near their homes.

I have been changed by this experience in ways that are difficult to describe. When I arrived at WKU, I wanted to understand environmental problems. Now, I want to solve them — or at least to contribute to the people and organisations who are doing so. I have applied for a Master's programme in environmental policy and intend to focus on industrial remediation in Central Asia. Despite the scale of the problem, I am not pessimistic. Although the challenges are enormous, they have been faced before — and progress has been made.

My grandfather, who is now eighty years old, asked me what I was studying when I last visited Karagandy. I told him I was studying the damage that the coal industry had done to the land and the air around the city. He was quiet for a moment. Then he said: "I am glad someone is doing that work." I think about that conversation often.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Aliya, your research sounds incredible. How did you get access to the mine sites?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: We had to apply for permission from the regional government. It took two months. Once we had the permit, we could collect samples freely.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Were the results what you expected?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: Worse, actually. We had expected elevated levels, but some sites were far above the legal limits. That was sobering.

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: More than we expected. The audit recommendation was adopted within three months. That rarely happens that quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: What would you say to a student who wanted to do similar research?

dialogue.speaker: Aliya
dialogue.text: Start with a question that genuinely matters to you. The work is too hard if you don't care about the answer.

keyPhrases.context: "The contamination had not been remediated." = cleaned up and returned to safe levels.
"Elevated levels of heavy metals." = above normal or safe concentrations.
"That was sobering." = made her think seriously; a humbling realisation.
"An independent audit of former mine sites." = an official examination of conditions.
"Industrial remediation." = cleaning up and restoring contaminated land.
"The contamination had not been remediated." = harmful substances in the environment.
"I am not pessimistic." = not expecting things to be bad; hopeful.
"I intend to focus on industrial remediation." = plan and aim to.

vocab.definition: to clean up or fix environmental damage
vocab.example: The contaminated soil had not been remediated despite the mine closing years ago.

vocab.definition: the presence of harmful substances in the environment
vocab.example: Heavy metal contamination near the former mine sites was above safe limits.

vocab.definition: causing you to think seriously; humbling
vocab.example: "That was sobering." — worse results than expected made the team think seriously.

vocab.definition: an official examination of an organisation or site
vocab.example: An independent audit of former mine sites will be conducted next year.

vocab.definition: tending to see the worst side of things; without hope
vocab.example: "I am not pessimistic." — Aliya remains hopeful despite the scale of problems.

vocab.definition: to plan or aim to do something
vocab.example: "I intend to focus on industrial remediation in Central Asia."

vocab.definition: a light fog or smoke obscuring the air
vocab.example: "A grey haze hung over the city." = pollution making the air grey and unclear.
"The results were striking." — far worse than expected; very notable.

questions.text: Why did Aliya choose to study environmental science?
opts: To understand and address environmental problems she observed growing up
questions.correct: To understand and address environmental problems she observed growing up
questions.hint: "I came to WKU to study environmental science because I wanted to understand what was happening... and to do something about it."

questions.text: What did the research team discover about the former mine sites?
opts: Heavy metal contamination was below legal limits
Contamination was above legal limits though mines closed 20+ years ago
questions.correct: Contamination was above legal limits though mines closed 20+ years ago
questions.hint: "Heavy metal concentrations in the soil were significantly above safe limits... the mines had been closed for over twenty years... the contamination had not been remediated."

questions.text: The Environment Agency rejected Aliya's team's recommendations.
questions.hint: "Two of our recommendations have since been adopted." — the Agency accepted them.

questions.text: What was the first recommendation that was adopted?
opts: An independent audit of former mine sites
questions.correct: An independent audit of former mine sites
questions.hint: "An independent audit of former mine sites in the region will be conducted next year."

questions.text: What does Aliya say about her outlook on environmental challenges?
opts: She is not pessimistic — progress has been made before
questions.correct: She is not pessimistic — progress has been made before
questions.hint: "Despite the scale of the problem, I am not pessimistic. Although the challenges are enormous, they have been faced before."

questions.text: Aliya's grandfather said he was ___ someone was doing that work.
questions.hint: "I am glad someone is doing that work." — Aliya's grandfather's response.

questions.text: What Past Perfect tense is used in: "By the time we submitted our findings, we had been working for three months."?
questions.hint: "had been working" = Past Perfect Continuous — duration up to a past moment. ✅

questions.text: "The contamination had not been remediated." — This passive form is:
questions.hint: "had not been remediated" = Past Perfect Passive (had + been + past participle). Earlier past action. ✅

questions.text: "Although the challenges are enormous, they have been faced before." "Although" signals:
opts: Contrast — acknowledging difficulty while staying hopeful
questions.correct: Contrast — acknowledging difficulty while staying hopeful
questions.hint: "Although" = contrast/concession. Acknowledges enormous challenges while contrasting with the hopeful message. ✅

questions.text: "Furthermore, I have completed two research internships." "Furthermore" signals:
questions.hint: "Furthermore" = addition. Adds "two internships" to the list of what Aliya has done. ✅

questions.text: "___ she had studied every day, she still failed." Choose.
questions.hint: "ALTHOUGH she had studied..." — full clause (she + had studied). Contrast marker. ✅

questions.text: "___ studying every day, she still failed." Choose.
questions.hint: "DESPITE studying" — gerund (no separate subject). ✅

questions.text: "The results were striking. ___, the team published immediately."
questions.hint: Cause → effect: THEREFORE / AS A RESULT / CONSEQUENTLY. ✅

questions.text: "The mines had already been closed ___ the results were analysed."
questions.hint: "...had already been CLOSED before the results were analysed." — time sequencer + Past Perfect. ✅

questions.text: "Samples ___ (collect) from ten sites." (Past Simple Passive)
questions.hint: "Samples WERE COLLECTED" = Past Simple Passive. ✅

questions.text: "A monitoring programme ___ (establish) now." (Present Continuous Passive)
questions.hint: "IS BEING ESTABLISHED" = Present Continuous Passive (is/are + being + pp). Ongoing now. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ (apply) for a Master's programme." (already done, result now)
questions.hint: Completed with present relevance → Present Perfect: "She HAS APPLIED for a Master's." ✅

questions.text: "I intend to focus ___ industrial remediation." Correct preposition:
questions.hint: "intend to focus ON [topic]." ✅ "Focus on" = give attention to.

questions.text: "Emissions must be reduced." — "must be reduced" is:
questions.hint: "must be reduced" = modal + be + past participle = Modal Passive. ✅

questions.text: "By the time she graduated, she ___ two internships." Choose.
questions.hint: "By the time + PS → Past Perfect." "She HAD COMPLETED two internships by the time she graduated." ✅

questions.text: "The contamination had not been remediated." "Remediated" means:
opts: Cleaned up and restored to safe levels
questions.correct: Cleaned up and restored to safe levels
questions.hint: "remediate" = to clean up environmental damage; restore to safe conditions.

questions.text: "The results were striking." "Striking" means:
questions.hint: "striking" = very noticeable; making a strong impression.

questions.text: "That was sobering." "Sobering" means:
opts: Making you think seriously about a difficult reality
questions.correct: Making you think seriously about a difficult reality
questions.hint: "sobering" = causing you to think seriously; a humbling or serious experience.

questions.text: "I intend to focus on remediation." "Intend" means:
questions.hint: "intend" = to have a plan or aim to do something. A deliberate intention.

questions.text: "I am not pessimistic." "Pessimistic" means:
questions.hint: "pessimistic" = tending to see the worst side; expecting bad outcomes.
